name: China Manufacturing Scale
narrative: IFR reports that factories in China installed about 354,000 industrial robots in 2025, or 59% of global annual installations; the United States installed almost 38,500. Chinese suppliers accounted for 55% of China's domestic installations. Capital follows the same pattern: Crunchbase counts $13.2 billion of robotics venture funding in China in the first nine months of 2026 against $12.1 billion in the U.S., excluding defense companies. Unitree, now listed on the STAR Market, reported Q3 revenue of RMB 665 million, up about 70%.

key_metrics.name: China share of global industrial installations

recommended_actions: Manufacturing capex incentives stacking with bonus depreciation
Federal procurement preference for US-made systems (HR 8189)
Supply-chain support for actuators, batteries, lidar where China dominates upstream
Visa pathway expansion for robotics talent

name: Robotics Foundation Models
narrative: Robotics foundation-model developers aim to use shared models across tasks and robot bodies. Skild AI raised a $1.4 billion Series C at a valuation above $14 billion in January 2026. Bloomberg reported in October that Physical Intelligence was in talks to raise at about a $20 billion valuation; the company has not confirmed it. Google put Gemini Robotics-ER 2, a planning model that checks task progress from video, into public preview on Google Cloud. Company demonstrations and reported results do not establish performance across all workplaces.

key_metrics.name: Skild AI valuation at Series C (more than)
Physical Intelligence reported valuation in talks

narrative_sources.label: Skild AI — Series C and S1
Bloomberg via PANews — Physical Intelligence talks

recommended_actions: Compute access programs for academic + small-firm robotics ML (analogue of NAIRR)
Open-source model + dataset support via NSF
Light-touch on foundation-model regulation pending NIST AI RMF maturity

name: Humanoid Cost Trajectory
narrative: 1X began taking preorders for its NEO home robot in October 2025 at $20,000 for early-access ownership, with a separate $499 monthly subscription option. Unitree’s G1 was introduced at a $16,000 starting price in 2024. Prices, subscription terms, capabilities and service costs differ, so these offers do not measure total industrial deployment cost.
recommended_actions: Demand-side incentives via enacted bonus depreciation for qualifying equipment
Pilot-risk-sharing fund for first-of-its-kind robot deployments per RFA framework

name: Defense Robotics Procurement
narrative: The Department of Defense launched Replicator to accelerate fielding of autonomous systems. In May 2024 it said about $500 million was secured for FY2024 and requested a roughly equal amount for FY2025; the earlier goal of multiple thousands of systems was a fielding target, not a verified count here. Replicator 2 shifted attention to countering small uncrewed aerial systems. H.R. 8189 remains a tracked proposal.
recommended_actions: Sustain DIU + Replicator funding through next defense authorization
Pass HR 8189 to lock in domestic procurement for sensitive applications
Accelerate ITAR clarifications for dual-use robotics components

name: Industrial Humanoid Deployment Wave
narrative: North American robot orders rose 24.8% in Q3 2026 to 10,989 units, A3 reports, led by automotive components and electronics. In humanoids, GXO and Agility plan Digit deployments at two more U.S. sites from early 2027, Foxconn's industrial unit says more than 10 humanoids work at its Texas sites, and Korean outlet KED reports Boston Dynamics asked suppliers to prepare for 10,000 Atlas units. Walmart's expanded Symbotic deal commits about $6 billion to automate 25 U.S. distribution centers. Planned sites and supplier preparations are not operating deployments.

narrative_sources.label: Reuters via Investing.com — Foxconn humanoids in Texas

recommended_actions: Pilot-risk-sharing fund — defray cost of first-of-its-kind deployments
Workforce co-investment to fund operator training alongside deployments
Safety standard clarification via NIST/OSHA for human-robot shared workspaces

name: Federal Policy Momentum
narrative: On October 28 the President found that imports of robots and industrial machinery threaten national security but imposed no tariff, directing Commerce and USTR to negotiate with trading partners and report within 180 days (Proclamation 11077). Treasury's October 26 outbound-investment proposal names humanoid, quadruped and industrial robots among covered AI systems; comments close December 7. The FCC's Covered List restriction on foreign robots is in effect, with conditional exemptions granted to robots whose makers commit to U.S. production plans.
recommended_actions: Track HR 7334 markup schedule — likely a leading indicator of broader federal alignment
Track IRS guidance for eligible automation equipment under enacted Public Law 119-21
Track FCC conditional approvals and the Section 232 robotics negotiations (update due 2027-04-26)

name: Physical AI ("AI with a body")
narrative: Physical AI combines AI with sensing and action in physical environments. Skild AI introduced its S1 model in August 2026 and reports more than $100 million in annual recurring revenue; Google's Gemini Robotics-ER 2 is in public preview with Boston Dynamics among named users. Crunchbase counts $9.9 billion of robotics venture funding in Q3 2026, up from $4.3 billion a year earlier. These are developer-reported results and funding totals, not independent evidence of general performance across workplaces.

key_metrics.name: Skild reported annual recurring revenue (more than)

narrative_sources.label: Skild AI — reported customers and revenue

recommended_actions: Treat robot foundation models as dual-use; track compute + data access alongside the AI Action Plan
Fund shared real-world robot data / sim infrastructure (NSF / NAIRR analogue) so value is not captured only by the best-capitalized labs
Watch foreign capital concentration in physical-AI startups for supply-chain + national-security exposure

name: US Robot Component Supply Chain
narrative: Robot manufacturing depends on motors, actuators, sensors, batteries and electronics. Westmag says its South San Francisco motor and actuator factory is ramping; Foundry Robotics raised $100 million to build an AI-driven assembly factory; and Re:Build raised $2.1 billion to expand U.S. hard-tech manufacturing. The Section 232 proclamation covers robot parts and components but sets no tariff yet. KED reports Boston Dynamics' Atlas supplier list is led by Korean firms, with Hyundai Mobis on actuators. Company-reported stages are not proof of output at scale.
recommended_actions: Extend NDAA Section 889 restrictions to robot actuators and servo motors sourced from adversary nations
Review potential Section 232 measures for precision gear reducers and brushless motors
Manufacturing capex tax credit (IRA-style) for US actuator and motor production
DoD Strategic & Critical Materials program should add servo motors and torque sensors to the monitored list
NIST / DoC supply-chain map of US robotic-component dependencies — public transparency on single points of failure
